name: Catherine Gitonga
bioShort: Catherine is an enterprise and business development expert with over 18 years of experience strengthening MSMEs across Eastern Africa, and Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Smart Regional Consultants since 2012.
bio:
Catherine is an enterprise and business development expert with over 18 years of experience strengthening MSMEs across Eastern Africa, and Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Smart Regional Consultants since 2012.

She specialises in business development services, investor readiness, market and financial linkages, market assessments and enterprise ecosystem analysis, with deep operating experience in arid and semi-arid and refugee-hosting counties including Turkana (Kakuma and Kalobeyei), Marsabit, Wajir, Isiolo, Samburu and Garissa.

She has led multi-donor assignments for USAID, the World Bank, FCDO, FAO, GIZ, IFC, Palladium, the IKEA Foundation, the Mastercard Foundation, ANDE, CARE and KCB Foundation. Current engagements include the FAO CASHA programme reaching 46,000 youth and women across 15 ASAL counties and the CARE SheConnects Digital Inclusion Accelerator targeting 20,000 women in trade in Isiolo and Marsabit.

Executive MBA, Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology; Bachelor of Education (Science), Egerton University. Member of the Aspen Network of Development Entrepreneurs (ANDE) and the Association of Startup and SME Enablers of Kenya (ASSEK).

name: Florence Ndwiga
bioShort: Monitoring, evaluation and learning expert with over 10 years of experience, complemented by more than five years in entrepreneurship training and mentorship.
bio:
Monitoring, evaluation and learning expert with over 10 years of experience, complemented by more than five years in entrepreneurship training and mentorship. She has worked with Smart Regional Consultants since July 2015, where she established the firm’s monitoring and evaluation system and has led MEL across the BOMA LIFT Northern Kenya and SEED programmes, the Invest in Africa investor readiness programme, GIZ Business Scouts for Development, Kenya RAPID, the USAID Livestock Market Systems programme and REGAL-AG.

She is skilled in quantitative and qualitative research design, survey programming using ODK-based platforms (SurveyCTO, KoBo, EpiCollect) and analysis in STATA, SPSS and Excel. Her evaluation portfolio includes baseline, mid-term and end-term assignments for IFC, ILO, SNV, World Vision, the World Food Programme, HelpAge International, Save the Children, Catholic Relief Services, IOM, Lutheran World Federation and the University of Nairobi/CDC, delivered across Kenya, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Mozambique and Zimbabwe.

Diploma in Monitoring and Evaluation, Kenya Institute of Management; Bachelor of Science in Foods, Nutrition and Dietetics (Second Class Honours, Upper Division), Kenyatta University; Master of Public Health (ongoing), Kenyatta University. SIYB (ILO) and Wadhwani Foundation certified entrepreneurship trainer.

name: Bonano Badia
bioShort: Bonano is a development finance specialist with two decades of experience in project finance, investment analysis, corporate finance and rural and MSME credit structuring. He joined Smart Regional Consultants in May 2024 to lead programme strategy, business development and cooperatives development.
bio:
Bonano is a development finance specialist with two decades of experience in project finance, investment analysis, corporate finance and rural and MSME credit structuring. He joined Smart Regional Consultants in May 2024 to lead programme strategy, business development and cooperatives development.

He previously served as Head of Operations and Chief Credit Officer at the Agricultural Finance Corporation, managing a credit portfolio of Ksh 10.37 billion across 48 branches and six regions with a staff complement of over 350, and has appraised more than 13,000 debt financing projects across agricultural value chains. He led formulation and implementation of the AFC Strategic Plan 2018/2022 and mainstreamed the AfDB-led Prudential Standards, Guidelines and Rating System, under which the Corporation moved from a D rating in 2011 to AA in 2019. 

He also served as Programme Manager of the Ksh 2.2 billion AfDB-funded ENABLE Youth Kenya programme and has mobilised major facilities from IFAD, FSD Kenya, AGRA, the Kenya Sugar Board and the Government of Kenya.

Master of Science in Finance and Investments and Bachelor of Arts in Economics, University of Nairobi; Certified Public Accountant, Strathmore University.

name: Emmaculate Mulinge
bioShort: Human resource and organisational development specialist covering talent acquisition and retention, performance management, culture change, and gender, youth and social inclusion.
bio:
Human resource and organisational development specialist covering talent acquisition and retention, performance management, culture change, and gender, youth and social inclusion. She has led the People and Culture strategy at Smart Regional Consultants since January 2026, spanning recruitment and selection, onboarding, learning and development, staff wellness, policy development, employee relations, compensation and benefits, and organisational change management.

She previously served as Senior Human Resource Specialist on USAID STAWI (DAI) and Human Resource Officer on the UNES/USAID HealthIT project. Her consultancy record includes executive and large-scale public sector recruitment: CEO and senior management searches for the Geothermal Development Company, board member recruitment for Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company, and psychometric and aptitude assessment of over 3,000 candidates for the Retirement Benefits Authority, the Office of the Auditor General, the National Mining Corporation and the Kenya Vision 2030 Secretariat. She has also led employee satisfaction, culture index and change management assignments for NEMA, RBA and LAPFUND, and mentored youth with disabilities under the Motivation Charitable Trust Leading, Willing and Able project.

Master of Commerce in Strategic Management, Strathmore University; Bachelor of Science in Human Resource Management, Moi University. Certified Human Resource Professional (HRMPEB) and member of the Institute of Human Resource Management Kenya

name: Caroline Nyagah
bioShort: Caroline is a finance leader with 24 years of experience in international NGO and development finance, serving as Head of Finance at Smart Regional Consultants since February 2023.
bio:
Caroline is a finance leader with 24 years of experience in international NGO and development finance, serving as Head of Finance at Smart Regional Consultants since February 2023. Her career includes 13 years rising through World Concern International to Africa Region Finance Manager and Regional Grant and Compliance Manager, followed by Associate Director for Grants, Finance and Fundraising at Farm Concern International and Grants and Finance Manager at the Drylands Learning and Capacity Building Initiative.

She brings proven strength in donor budgeting and grants compliance across USAID, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, FCDO, the European Union, United Nations bodies and the Government of Kenya, together with treasury and cash flow management, internal controls, audit management and board reporting. She has managed portfolios of up to USD 10 million and led fundraising resulting in grants ranging from USD 100,000 to USD 6 million. Country experience spans Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Somalia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Chad.

Certified Public Accountant, CPA(K), Strathmore College; Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Business Studies, Kenyatta University; MBA in Strategic Management (ongoing), Africa Nazarene University. Member of ICPAK and Humentum. Serves on three boards, including as Chair of the Finance Committee at World Concern International.

In this role, he ensures that program activities are delivered efficiently, in line with set objectives, and in alignment with organizational standards. Lomosingo holds a Bachelor of Science in Entomology and Parasitology from the University of Eldoret. With five years of experience in humanitarian work, research, and project management, he has contributed to the success of several impactful initiatives, including Kuza Jamii, an FCDO-funded project, and Kenya Young African Works, implemented by the KCB Foundation. Through this work, he has developed strong expertise in coordinating multi-stakeholder programs, building the capacity of local actors, and delivering results that respond to community needs.

Lomosingo is passionate about creating lasting impact in the communities he engages with, particularly through projects that promote sustainability and resilience. He believes that empowering individuals and enterprises with the right skills and support is key to driving long-term change. His approachable and collaborative style allows him to work effectively with teams, partners, and community members alike.

Outside of work, Lomosingo enjoys playing football and pool, activities that reflect his team spirit and love of friendly competition.
